title: Support escalation template + automation hooks for Dedicated throughput complaints
creator: Owen Phillips
description:
## Context
Support and CS are already getting "throughput is lower than promised" tickets (Dedicated) and we’re spending cycles in back-and-forth to collect the minimum information needed to determine:
- Is this an SLO miss (per measurement standard), expected throttling/admission control, or customer-side load pattern change?
- If it’s platform-side, is it runtime (scheduling), infra (shape saturation / noisy neighbor shouldn’t happen but still needs validation), or fleet capacity (burst exhausted / wrong tier)?

We need a standardized escalation template + lightweight automation so Support can file a high-signal escalation on first contact, with dashboard/log links attached.

This ticket implements the engineering pieces for Support-readiness:
- A canonical intake template (Jira fields + description block)
- A link generator (dashboards/logs/traces) based on deployment_id and time window
- A "minimum viable" automation hook to attach those links to the ticket

References:
- Confluence draft playbook: `customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/dedicated-throughput-slo-escalation`
- Dashboards spec: `eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/dedicated-throughput-slo-dashboards`
- Metrics instrumentation: ENG-2194
- Dashboards/alerts buildout: ENG-2201

## Goal
Make Dedicated throughput complaints actionable within 15 minutes of intake by ensuring each escalation contains:
1) The exact measurement window and customer expectation
2) Deployment + tier + shape details
3) A reproducible view of throughput SLI + throttling + queue depth for that window
4) Enough workload context to interpret results (streaming vs non-streaming, model, context-length distribution, concurrency)

## Non-goals
- Designing the full Support workflow in Jira (Support owns final UX); we provide the template + required fields + automation.
- Building a new observability UI; we link to Grafana/Logs/Traces.
- Replacing the oncall runbook; we link to the existing overload mitigation runbook.

## Deliverables
### A) Jira escalation template (Dedicated throughput)
Add a template block Support can paste/use (and optionally convert into a Jira “Request type” in SUP project).

**Template sections (exact fields):**
1. Customer + environment
   - Customer org / account (HubSpot ID if available)
   - Dedicated deployment_id (required)
   - Tier (Standard/Performance/Premium) (required)
   - Region (required)
   - Shape (GPU type/count, MIG on/off if applicable)
   - Model + version (required)

2. Incident window
   - Start time (UTC) (required)
   - End time (UTC) (required)
   - Is this ongoing? (Y/N)
   - Did Support verify clock alignment with customer? (Y/N)

3. Customer expectation and what changed
   - What throughput did the customer expect (tokens/sec or req/sec) and where did that expectation come from? (contract, proposal, prior observed, internal statement)
   - What are they observing now? (include screenshots or numbers)
   - First seen timestamp
   - Any known changes: prompt size distribution, model change, traffic ramp, new features (tools/function calling), streaming enabled, etc.

4. Workload characteristics (last 1h during window)
   - Streaming: on/off
   - Typical input tokens (p50/p95) (best-effort)
   - Typical output tokens (p50/p95) (best-effort)
   - Concurrency: average + peak
   - Request mix: chat vs completion vs embeddings (should be mostly chat/completion for this queue)
   - Any rate limiting or client retries observed

5. Platform signals (links auto-generated; see section B)
   - Grafana: Throughput SLI (effective output tok/s) panel link pinned to window
   - Grafana: Throttling rate (429/admission control) panel link pinned to window
   - Grafana: Queue depth / scheduler backlog panel link pinned to window
   - Grafana: GPU saturation / memory pressure link pinned to window
   - Logs query link for deployment_id pinned to window
   - Trace explorer link (if sampling available) pinned to window

6. Preliminary classification (Support selection)
   - Likely expected throttling (burst exceeded / concurrency above tier assumptions)
   - Possible SLO breach
   - Unsure

7. Escalation routing
   - Page SRE now? (Y/N; criteria below)
   - Assign Runtime? (Y/N)
   - Assign Infra/Fleet? (Y/N)

**Paging criteria (for Support):**
- Page SRE if ongoing + customer reports production impact AND throughput SLI < objective for > 30 min AND throttling rate is low (i.e., not an expected throttle-only event).
- Do NOT page if the primary signal is high throttling with stable platform health; route to CS/PM for tier sizing discussion unless customer has Premium + burst clause.

### B) Link generator (dashboard/log/traces)
Implement a small internal helper (can be a script + docs, or a lightweight endpoint under existing internal tooling) that accepts:
- deployment_id
- start/end (UTC)
- region (optional; derive if possible)

…and outputs a copy-pastable block with:
- Grafana dashboard deep links with time range
- Loki (or logging backend) query link filtered to deployment_id
- Trace explorer link filtered to deployment_id (if supported)

**Notes:**
- Links must not include customer content (prompts/completions). Queries should be scoped to metadata fields only.
- Ensure we don’t generate links that require elevated permissions beyond what Support/SRE already has.

### C) Automation hook
Minimum: a Slack workflow / internal bot command that:
- Prompts Support for deployment_id + time window
- Returns the link block (from section B)

Stretch: Jira automation that injects the link block into the ticket description when the required fields are present.

## Implementation plan
1) Define the canonical field names and labels to match the metrics taxonomy (deployment_id, tier, region, model). Coordinate with Sergio (ENG-2201) so dashboard variables match the template.
2) Add the link generator as a small utility:
   - Start as a repo script under `observability/support/throughput_escalation_links.py` (or similar)
   - Document usage in the escalation playbook
3) Provide the Jira template text in Confluence (source of truth) + pasteable snippet in Linear.
4) Pilot with Support on 2–3 real tickets (e.g., SUP-4821 style) and iterate.

## Acceptance criteria
- Support can create a Dedicated throughput escalation with all required fields in < 10 minutes.
- Link generator produces correct, time-pinned Grafana links for a known deployment_id.
- At least one real ticket is filed using the template and successfully triaged without requesting additional basic data (deployment_id, time window, tier/model).
- No customer content is included in logs/traces links generated by the tool.

## Open questions
- Do we want Support to capture customer-side measurements (client tok/s) in a structured field, or freeform?
- For multi-model deployments (fallback policies), do we require the exact model used, or is `model_family` sufficient for first-pass triage?
- Trace availability: do Support users have access to Tempo/trace explorer today, or should that link be SRE-only?

## Risks
- Cardinality/perms: dashboard variables must remain safe (deployment_id can be high-cardinality). We should rely on existing per-deployment dashboards rather than ad-hoc queries when possible.
- Confusion between "guarantee" vs "observed" throughput. Template explicitly asks where expectation came from to avoid contract disputes being routed as incidents.

## Output artifacts
- Confluence snippet (final) for the escalation template
- Script/tool for link generation + README
- Slack workflow/bot command description for Support
comments: 2025-02-11 — Owen Phillips: Support is getting more Dedicated throughput tickets; we need a template with required fields + an easy way to attach dashboard links. The current back-and-forth (deployment_id, time range, tier, streaming) is burning hours. Can we get something usable by end of month?

2025-02-12 — Logan Wright: Agreed. I can own the link generator and coordinate with Sergio so the dashboard variables match. Question: are we standardizing on effective output tok/s for the SLI panels? (Assuming yes per ADR-0127.)

2025-02-13 — Aisha Bello: Please include a clear paging criteria section. We’ve been paged for cases that are simply admission control doing its job. Paging should require low throttling + sustained SLI below objective for >=30m (unless Premium + customer claims outage).

2025-02-14 — Sergio Costa: Dashboard work (ENG-2201) will have deployment_id + time window deep link support. If you generate URLs, keep them pointing at the Dedicated Throughput SLO dashboard and pass vars: deployment_id, region, model (optional).

2025-02-18 — Logan Wright: Drafted the template text and a first version of the link generator script (local). Next step is deciding where it should live for Support to use without cloning repos—leaning Slack command wrapper that runs in our internal tooling environment.

2025-02-20 — Owen Phillips: Prefer Slack workflow (Support already uses it during intake). Jira automation can be phase 2. Also need explicit instruction: do NOT attach raw request/response logs; only metadata + platform counters.

2025-02-24 — Logan Wright: Added guardrails: logs query restricted to `deployment_id` + `request_id` + `status_code` + scheduler events; no payload fields. Need final confirmation from SRE that Support has access to the logging UI in all regions.

2025-02-26 — Rafael Mendes: SRE reviewed. Looks good. One tweak: add a field for whether the customer is using streaming, because it changes how they perceive "throughput" vs latency. Also include a checkbox for "customer changed prompt sizes" (common root cause). Marking ready for final review after docs land in Confluence.
